title: Introduce per-route/model/region p95 & p99 latency metrics and Grafana dashboards
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add first-class p95 and p99 latency tracking and dashboards broken down by API route, model, and region. Provide regression detection hooks so load tests and daily baselines can trigger alerts when tail latency degrades. Deliverables: Prometheus recording rules, Grafana dashboard with per-route/model/region panels, CI job integration for load harness, and alerting/automation for regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Prometheus recording rules expose p95 and p99 per route/model/region (queryable and cheap to evaluate)
Grafana dashboard with overview and drilldowns: overall cluster p95/p99, per-route matrix, per-model rows, and per-region columns
Regression detection: automated alert when p95 increases by >10% vs 7-day baseline OR absolute p99 > config threshold
Load test job in CI can produce tokens/sec, p95, p99 and upload artifact snapshots to S3 for historical comparison
Runbook updated: steps for triage, rollback policies, and mitigation knobs (route routing fallback, autoscale burst)
updates: 2026-02-25: Ticket created. Initial scoping meeting notes: aim to rely on existing OpenTelemetry + Prometheus pipeline. Avoid high-cardinality label explosion; route/model/region chosen as primary selectors.

2026-03-02: Prototype recording rules checked in to runtime repo (PR #987). Using histogram buckets on inference_request_latency_seconds with labels {route, model, region}. Early queries for histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(...[5m])) look stable in staging.

2026-03-05: Load harness run against staging (k6 custom driver). Baseline p95 by route collected; found one model-route (chat-compress/v1 - /v1/chat) exhibiting 28% higher p95 when region=eu-west vs us-west under identical tokens/sec load. Added tuning task to investigate batching horizon and KV cache warmup for that model in eu-west.

2026-03-10: Grafana dashboard draft created (folder: runtime/perf/p95-p99). Added panel templates and per-route templating variables. Feedback from PM and SRE: prefer per-model drilldown and linked trace for slow p99 samples (OpenTelemetry trace_id annotation).

2026-03-13: Regression detection design reviewed with SRE and Product. Decision: record daily 7-day rolling median and flag >10% increase in p95 sustained for 3 evaluation windows (5m windows). Alert channels: #perf-alerts slack + PagerDuty for P0 customers impact. Implementing recording rules and two Grafana alerts next sprint.

2026-03-14: Work in progress on CI integration. Load job stores JSON artifact to s3://redwood-perf-artifacts/ENG-4821/2026-03-14.json and triggers comparison job that computes delta vs baseline. Preparing PR for alerting rules and dashboard finalization.
implementation_notes: Metrics: add/standardize 'inference_request_latency_seconds' as Prometheus histogram with labels: route, model, region, instance_type. Keep cardinality low by restricting model tag to canonical model id (no hash variants).

Use histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, model, region)) to compute p95 per dimension. For p99 use 0.99. Avoid summaries for cardinality reasons.
Recording rules: create 'record: p95_request_latency_seconds:hist:rate5m' and 'p99_request_latency_seconds:hist:rate5m' that are precomputed to reduce Grafana query load.

Dashboards: top-level: cluster p95/p99, tokens/sec heatmap, error-rate. Drilldown boards filtered by route, model, region. Panels include: time-series p95/p99, distribution violin for tail latency, tokens/sec vs latency scatter, and recent slow traces linked via trace_id.

Regression detection: baseline = 7-day rolling median of p95 for a (route, model, region). Alert if (current_p95 - baseline)/baseline > 0.10 and sustained for 3 consecutive 5m windows. Also alert if absolute p99 > per-model threshold configurable in defaults.yaml.

Load harness: extend existing k6 runner to parameterize model/route/region and emit tokens_sec, request_count, p50/p95/p99. CI pipeline stores artifact and runs 'compare_perf.py' to produce deltas and simple HTML report.
Storage: perf artifacts written to S3 with key pattern s3://redwood-perf-artifacts/<issue>/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<run-id>.json for historical regression audits.
Trace sampling: increase OTEL sampling to 5% for requests with latency > p95 to guarantee linkable traces for triage. Add trace_id label to error logs for quick correlation.

Cost trade-offs: histogram with many buckets increases DB pressure. We will start with coarse buckets tuned for 1ms..2s and iterate if p99 requires more granularity. Recording rules reduce repeated query cost at the expense of Prometheus recording CPU/time.
Rollout: feature flag 'perf_p95_p99_v1' to gate recording rules and dashboard exposure. Gradual rollout to staging then canary in us-west before global.

Fallbacks: when alerts fire, operations can: switch route to lower-capacity model variant, increase dedicated capacity for route, or enable stricter batching/kv-cache warmup TTL adjustments. Documented in runbook.
notes_for_reviewers: Please validate Prometheus queries for cost (cardinality) and confirm that the chosen labels won't explode. SRE: review alert thresholds and PD escalation logic. PM: confirm p95 delta thresholds align with SLOs for enterprise customers.
